title: 2.2 migrateIn bricks ALL stakers mid-migration after the terminal drain when the 2.1 in-place allotment is zero or under-sized — the 2.1 require(>0) tripwire is necessary but does not guarantee sufficiency
description: Step6 `migrateIn(DOLA/USDC, 0, max)` re-credits each parked staker via `depositFor(amt)`, which credits only the strategy's haircut-reduced return. The ERC4626 redeem-then-deposit round-trip realizes a small migration slippage EVEN ON SOLVENT POOLS (totalBalance > principal on the fork), so `credited < amt` for every staker and the surplus-funded gross-up top-up path fires. The top-up is funded from the migrator's surplus (`balance - totalParked`), which is exactly the DOLA_ALLOTMENT/USDC_ALLOTMENT transferred in 2.1. If that surplus is insufficient, `_reinjectWithTopup` reverts 'top-up surplus exhausted' (line 282) and the whole batch reverts. 2.1 hardcodes both allotments to 0 with a `require(>0)` tripwire — but the tripwire only proves non-zero, not sufficiency, and it lives in the PREDECESSOR script; the operator who sets 2.1's allotments has no in-script signal of the per-staker shortfall 2.2 will actually need.
impact: No theft — InPlaceMigrator invariant C (source-verified at lines 244, 320, 337-339) guarantees parked principal can only return to its original owner; `claimTimedOut` (lines 306-323) is a permissionless, self-only, principal-returning escape hatch any parked user can call unilaterally after the 14-day migrationTimeout. The lock is total but TEMPORARY, attacker-free, and SELF-CURING, so High (assets stolen/lost/compromised) is excluded. Impact is availability + a bounded value-leak: fork-confirmed, with ZERO allotment migrateIn(DOLA) reverts at step6 — AFTER pause (step1), skim (step2), `initiateMigration`+`migrateOut` (step4, TERMINAL — the staker pool can never resume healthy operation per stable-staker CLAUDE.md), and `finalizeAndReset`+`setYieldStrategy` (step6 rewire). The staker is left paused, terminally migrating, with ALL stakers' principal parked in the migrator and recoverable only via `claimTimedOut` after the 14-day timeout (principal-only, no further phUSD). The realized leak is the forgone phUSD/yield and the time-value of the 14-day lockup — in-motion/unmatured yield, independently capping this at Medium. Measured minimum allotment at block 25322425: ~0.0149 DOLA (3 stakers) + ~0.198 USDC (6 stakers); 1 wei is insufficient. Absolute cost is sub-dollar, but because 2.1 hardcodes both allotments to 0, the brick is the DEFAULT path absent a manual fix.
attackPath: 1. 2.1 sets DOLA/USDC allotment to a token >0 value that passes the require(>0) tripwire but is below the per-staker gross-up shortfall (fork floor ~0.0149 DOLA / ~0.198 USDC; 1 wei is insufficient).
2. 2.2 step1 pauses, step2 skims, step4 initiateMigration + migrateOut TERMINALLY drains the staker, step6 finalizeAndReset + setYieldStrategy rewires.

3. Step6 migrateIn re-credits each staker via depositFor; the ERC4626 redeem-then-deposit round-trip realizes a per-staker haircut even on solvent pools, so credited < amt and the surplus-funded gross-up fires.
4. Migrator surplus (== the 2.1 allotment) is exhausted; _reinjectWithTopup reverts 'top-up surplus exhausted'; the whole batch reverts.
5. Staker is left paused + terminally migrating with all principal parked; users wait 14 days for claimTimedOut (principal-only, no further phUSD).
recommendation: Add a 2.2 preflight assertion (before pause/drain) that the migrator holds a surplus >= a conservative bound on the per-staker gross-up shortfall (e.g. estimate via `previewRedeem`/`convertToAssets` round-trip on the new strategy for each token's parked principal), so an under-sized allotment aborts BEFORE engaging terminal migration. At minimum, document in 2.1 the empirically-measured shortfall (~0.015 DOLA / ~0.2 USDC at current pool sizes, scaling with staker count and pool drift) so the allotment is sized with margin, not just set to a token >0 value that passes the tripwire.
